pr_title: libnetwork: Always use an IPv4 to (re)create default bridge
pr_comments: PR https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/44827 fixes the issue reported in https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/44220. Closing.

issue_context.title: order in default-address-pools in daemon.json is relevant
issue_context.body:
### Description

using the list of `default-address-pools` in daemon.json in different orders leads to the configuration error:

```
failed to start daemon: Error initializing network controller: 
Error creating default "bridge" network: 
failed to parse pool request for address space "LocalDefault" pool "fc00:1337:1337::/80" subpool "127.16.0.0/12": 
failed to compute range's lowest ip address: 
cannot compute host portion ip address because ip and mask are not compatible: 
(net.IP{0x7f, 0x10, 0x0, 0x0}, net.IPMask{0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0, 0x0})
```

### Reproduce

Working order (ipv4 first):
```
  "default-address-pools": [
    {
      "base": "172.16.0.0/12",
      "size": 24
    },
    {
      "base": "fc00:1337:1337::0/64",
      "size": 80
    }
```

Broken order (ipv6 first):
```
  "default-address-pools": [
    {
      "base": "fc00:1337:1337::0/64",
      "size": 80      
    },
    {
      "base": "172.16.0.0/12",
      "size": 24
    }
```

### Expected behavior

a list in json configuration should not be order dependent

comments:
I tried to reproduce this issue, and although I don't see the same error messages I can confirm the daemon fails to start when an IPv6 subnet is put before IPv4 subnet(s):

> failed to start daemon: Error initializing network controller: Error creating default "bridge" network: failed to add IPv4 address fc00:1337:1337::1/8

Didn't went down the rabbit hole yet, but I tested #43033 and I confirm this PR is fixing the issue.

EDIT: Will publish a fix for that tomorrow.

review_comments: This call to `netutils.FindAvailableNetwork` is being passed a list of length 1. It's used to check whether the pool—singular—returned from `ipam.RequestPool` would conflict with routes in use on the host. The call to `ipam.RequestPool` specifies the address family (IPv4 vs. IPv6), so the question is: why do we have to double-check that `ipam.RequestPool` respected the request? Seems like we should be fixing the root cause, the bug in the IPAM allocator which allocates IPv6 pools when an IPv4 pool is requested.
